messages:
toni: Heads-up — hitting reproducible mem growth + fragmentation in kvcache on long-context tests across H100/A100/RTX. Dumping notes.

toni: Repro: run `./tools/test_longctx --model llama-7b --seq 1M --gpu a100` then stream many requests, observe steady GPU mem climb and kvcache hole count increase.

toni: Profiler snippet:
```
KVCache: total_pages=32768 used=31200 free=2568 hole_count=184
GPU mem: 56GB -> 61GB over 90s
kernel selection: matmul_fused_v2 (h100) vs matmul_v1 (a100)
page_walks: 1.2M evicts: 24k reclaim_fail: 18
```

rajiv: ugh. does the hole_count go down after GC? any evict ordering logs?

toni: no, hole_count monotonically increases. Evict logs show many "deferred-evict" entries. here's the snippet from kvcache log:
```
[evict] id=0x1a2 evict_page=4092 owner=stream-7 deferred=1
[map] vaddr=0x7ff... mapped page=4092 owner=stream-9
[evict] id=0x1a2 released but owner still refs=1
```

bench-bot: nightly/longctx-regress failed on h100-3 (test id 2026-03-17-llm-longctx). See https://ci.redwood/example/2026-03-17 :eyes: 

emily: @toni can you try toggling KV_PAGE_COMPACT=1 env var? last time compaction raced with concurrent map updates and left stale PTEs.

toni: tried compaction on/off. with COMPACT=1 the hole_count still grows but slower. with COMPACT=0 it jumps faster. suspect reuse window and partial remap race.

rajiv: could be a missing write memory barrier between page_table update + gpu binding. h100 driver reorder semantics differ from a100. Do you have the GPU fence traces?

toni: attached fence trace excerpt:
```
fence submit=12345 complete=12344
map op ts=12346 queued after complete
```

toni: also saw different kernel chosen on h100 for kv-read which does streaming loads instead of vectorized gather — might leave a stale cache state when pages are swapped back.

emily: try setting KV_EVICT_SERIAL=1 and rerun on h100. serial eviction avoids concurrent free->remap races. :+1:

toni: ran with KV_EVICT_SERIAL=1 — hole_count stabilizes and mem plateaued at 57GB. repro still triggers on a few runs but much rarer.

rajiv: ok that strongly suggests an ordering/race. can you capture a minimal repro that reproduces with KV_EVICT_SERIAL=0 and not with 1? we'll need perf counters + CUs mapping.

toni: gj. I'll create a small harness that issues interleaved map/unmap patterns. Also hitting a reproducible segfault once when mixed VRAM allocations + peer-to-peer copies happen.

emily: filed issue #3124 and added the bench logs + trace: https://issues.redwood/3124

toni: plan: (1) minimal repro harness, (2) add explicit STW barrier when page_table->owner transitions, (3) test on h100/a100/rtx. assigning to @rajiv for kernel-order review.

rajiv: ack. I'll instrument page_table ops with atomic counters and add a tracepoint.

bench-bot: note: rolling back recent kvcache allocator refactor (PR 2456) reduced longctx failures by 30% in canary yesterday.

emily: if we confirm barrier fixes, add a perf test and enable KV_EVICT_SERIAL rollout guard until fixed.

toni: thanks all. I'll post the harness link when ready.
